title: Linear Table Format

illustrates.quote: Wide Tables: Linear Table Format. When other options are not effective in dealing with wide tables, a linear format may be used. Multiple columns of numbers or repetitive types of entries (e.g., proper names) are not appropriate for linear format. This format is not an option when there are colons or semicolons in the table. (See Sample 11-25: Linear Table Format on page 11-52.)

print.notes: Arkansas's Nickname cell is blank in print.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box, ruled line under the header row; header row bold.

braille.notes: Line 1 placeholder 'text'. A transcriber's note on lines 4-6 explains: a series of three dot 5s indicates a blank space in print, and columns follow one another in this order (per the rule's own sample sentence pattern). Line 8 lists the column-heading order with punctuation: 'State:' (colon after the first heading, rule c) then 'Capital;', 'Nickname;', 'Flower;', 'Bird' (semicolons after each internal heading). Each data row (lines 11, 13, 15, 17) then runs the row linearly: state name + colon, capital + semicolon, nickname + semicolon, flower + semicolon, bird - continuing onto a second, indented line (12, 14, 16, 18) when the row is too long for one line, per rule f/h. Arkansas's blank Nickname (line 17) is rendered as three unspaced dot-5 guide dots ('"""') followed by the semicolon, per rule k.
